title: Completeness characterization of locally presentable categories
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ and use ordinary categories with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets. All smallness below is relative to $\mathcal U$; object collections may belong to a larger universe. For an infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, a category is $\kappa$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms has a cocone. Regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ has size less than $\kappa$. An object $P$ is $\kappa$-presentable if $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. A category is accessible if, for some such $\kappa$, it has all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits and a small family of $\kappa$-presentable objects such that every object is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of that family. Colimits mean [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

Call a category locally presentable if it is accessible and has all small colimits. Call it complete if every small diagram $D:J\to\mathcal A$ admits a limiting cone: an object $L$ with compatible maps $p_j:L\to D(j)$ through which every cone factors uniquely. Call it cocomplete if it has all small colimits. For every category $\mathcal A$ the following three conditions are equivalent: $\mathcal A$ is accessible and complete; $\mathcal A$ is accessible and cocomplete; $\mathcal A$ is locally presentable.
